testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:338 — Re-authentication tests never exercise a failed conditional-WebAuthn assertion, leaving the new error-path reauthentication form setup unverified.

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is being called without the required UserModel parameter. The golden comment states the parameter is missing, while the candidate describes it as calling a 'nonexistent zero-argument overload' which would cause compilation failure. These are describing the exact same underlying problem - the method call is missing its required argument.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 — Requiring a non-null user suppresses conditional-passkey form setup on the initial anonymous login, removing passkey UI and challenge data.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment - that requiring a non-null user in the conditional passkeys check prevents the conditional-passkey form setup from being called on the initial anonymous login (when context.getUser() is null), which removes the passkey UI and challenge data needed for ID-less passkey authentication. Both comments point to the same bug at the same location (the isConditionalPasskeysEnabled check requiring user != null) and describe the same consequence (conditional passkey UI not being set up for first-time/anonymous passkey login).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/util/AuthenticatorUtils.java:35 — The generic utility now imports a browser authenticator's session-note constant, forcing that implementation detail public and creating a reverse package dependency.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that AuthenticatorUtils.java (a generic utility in the 'util' package) now imports USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH from AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator (a browser-specific authenticator). The diff shows the constant was changed from 'protected' to 'public' specifically to enable this import. This creates a reverse dependency where a utility class depends on a specific authenticator implementation, which is a legitimate architectural concern. The finding accurately describes what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:338 — Re-authentication tests never exercise a failed conditional-WebAuthn assertion, leaving the new error-path reauthentication form setup unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points out that the new tests for re-authentication don't test the error path where a WebAuthn/passkey assertion fails. Looking at the diff, the new method `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` was added in `AuthenticatorUtils.java` and is called from `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse()`. The new tests in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java` (like `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication` and `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`) test successful passkey authentication and password failures, but don't test what happens when a conditional WebAuthn assertion itself fails during re-authentication. This is a valid observation about missing test coverage for newly added error-handling code, though the tests do cover password authentication failures which exercise a related path.
